questions.explanation: Let first term = a, common difference = d. Number of terms = 2k. Last term = a + (2k-1)d. Given last - first = 27 ⇒ (2k-1)d = 27. Sum of odd terms: terms at positions 1,3,5,...,2k-1. There are k odd terms. These form an AP with first term a, common difference 2d. Sum = (k/2)[2a + (k-1)2d] = k[a + (k-1)d] = 40. Sum of even terms: terms at positions 2,4,...,2k. There are k terms, first term a+d, common difference 2d. Sum = (k/2)[2(a+d) + (k-1)2d] = k[(a+d) + (k-1)d] = k[a + kd] = 55. Subtract: k[a+kd] - k[a+(k-1)d] = 55-40 ⇒ kd = 15 ⇒ d = 15/k. Then (2k-1)(15/k) = 27 ⇒ 15(2k-1) = 27k ⇒ 30k - 15 = 27k ⇒ 3k = 15 ⇒ k = 5.
